sections.h2: How is Tennessee organized for a home sale?
sections.html:
Tennessee has 95 counties, and the county is where most of a house sale gets recorded and taxed. Cities and towns sit inside that county layer. The state counts 346 municipalities, and three places run a merged city and county government: Nashville with Davidson County, Lynchburg with Moore County, and Hartsville with Trousdale County.

That matters because the office you call depends on the address. The county register of deeds records the deed. The county trustee collects county property tax. Some cities bill their own tax, and others hand collection to the trustee.

The list further down this page is arranged by county, so you can find your county first and then the city guides inside it. Our Tennessee guides by city and county page collects the same material in one place.

sections.h2: When are Tennessee property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
County taxes for the current year are due the first Monday in October, and March 1 is the delinquency date for the preceding year's bill. February 28 is the last day to pay without interest. Property is assessed as it stands on January 1 of each tax year.

If you disagree with the assessed value, the county board of equalization generally meets June 1 (Shelby County meets May 1), and the assessment records must be open to the public before May 20. Appeals to the State Board of Equalization are generally due August 1 or 45 days after the county board sends its notice, whichever is later.

A city that collects its own tax may set its own dates. Ask the trustee for a payoff figure before you set a closing date. Our Tennessee property tax guide covers appeals and selling with tax due in more detail.

  • County tax is collected by the county trustee.
  • Value disputes start at the county board of equalization.
  • Back tax can be paid at closing from the sale price.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Tennessee?
sections.html:
Tennessee charges a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, which works out to $370 on a $100,000 sale. The grantee, meaning the buyer, pays it. The county register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded and sends it on to the Department of Revenue.

A separate mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of debt applies to deeds of trust and similar loan papers, and the first $2,000 of the debt is exempt. A cash buyer with no new loan has no mortgage tax to pay. Recording fees are set by the county, so ask the register of deeds. See, for example, the Davidson County register of deeds and the Shelby County register of deeds.

sections.h2: Does Tennessee have a homestead exemption for sellers?
sections.html:
Yes, but it works against creditors, not against the tax bill. The statute caps the exemption at $35,000 for an individual, and joint owners using the home as their principal residence can claim a combined $52,500 when they claim in the same proceeding. It protects the home from execution, attachment or sale in legal proceedings during the owner's lifetime.

It does not apply against public taxes, debts for buying the home or improving it, or debts secured by the home where the exemption was waived in a written contract. A deed of trust or mortgage that conveys the property conveys it free of the exemption. See our homestead guide for how this differs from tax relief programs for older and disabled owners.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in Tennessee?
sections.html:
A sale under a deed of trust runs on published notice. Section 35-5-101 requires the notice to run at least twice in a newspaper in the county of the sale, with the first publication at least 20 days before the sale date. A third-party website must also post the notice online for at least 20 continuous days.

The trustee or selling party must mail a copy of the notice to the debtor and any co-debtor by registered or certified mail, on or before the first publication date. A sale can be postponed, and unless the contract forbids it, the new sale must happen within one year of the original date. If the delay is longer than 30 days, a new notice goes out by regular mail at least 10 calendar days before the sale.

  • Newspaper notice at least twice in the sale county.
  • Online posting for 20 continuous days.
  • Certified or registered mail to the debtor.
  • Postponements allowed within one year of the first date.

If a notice has already arrived, call an attorney first. Unpaid tax follows a different path, described in our tax sale guide.

sections.h2: How does an inherited house get sold in Tennessee?
sections.html:
It depends on the estate. A small estate under the Small Estates Act means personal property of no more than $50,000, and the affidavit cannot transfer title to real estate. A house therefore needs a regular probate process with a personal representative who has court authority before a deed is signed.

Creditors have a deadline too. Under section 30-2-310, claims not filed with the probate court clerk, or in suit, within 12 months of the date of death are generally barred, though claims for taxes are treated separately. Our estate tax guide covers inheritance tax. For the full process, read our probate guide and speak with a probate attorney or the clerk and master of the county where the owner lived.

sections.h2: What if a Tennessee house has tenants?
sections.html:
The rules depend on the county. The Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act applies to counties with more than 75,000 people by the 2010 census. The commentary lists Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson.

In those counties a tenant has 14 days to fix a curable breach after receiving notice, and a repeat breach within six months allows termination on 7 days' written notice. Rules in smaller counties differ, so the county clerk or an attorney should confirm the notice you need. Our guides on landlord and tenant law and eviction notices go further.

A buyer who pays cash for a house as-is may buy it with the tenant in place or after the tenant has moved out. Settle that point in the contract.

sections.h2: What property problems come up in Tennessee?
sections.html:
Radon and ground movement are the two the state itself flags. The state health program says radon can enter any home in Tennessee and that no zone is free of risk. The EPA action level is 4 pCi/L, and a result above it should be confirmed with a follow-up test before a fix is arranged. The state's radon program supplies test kits to homeowners.

The state emergency management agency notes that Tennessee's hills, valleys, caves and sinkholes make some areas more prone to landslides, rockfalls, sinkholes and unstable slopes. It points owners to cracks in foundations, walls and driveways as warning signs.

  • Run a radon test before listing, or tell a buyer you have not.
  • Look for foundation or driveway cracks after heavy rain.
  • Keep gutters and drainage clear of the foundation.

sections.h2: How does a cash as-is sale work in Tennessee?
sections.html:
You sell the house in its current condition, with no repairs, cleaning or staging, and the buyer pays with cash instead of a mortgage. That removes the loan approval and appraisal steps that slow many sales. Closing usually runs through a title company or attorney who checks the title, pays off liens, and records the deed with the county register of deeds.

The costs you still weigh are the same as any sale: the payoff on any mortgage, unpaid property tax, and the buyer's transfer tax, which the buyer pays. Ask a tax professional about any gain.

If you want to compare a cash offer with a listing, tell us the address and the situation. Our team buys houses in Tennessee and across the country, either directly or by bringing a vetted cash buyer.

faqs.q: How many counties does Tennessee have?
faqs.a: Tennessee has 95 counties. The county register of deeds records your deed, and the county trustee collects county property tax.

faqs.q: When are Tennessee property taxes due?
faqs.a: Current-year county tax is due the first Monday in October. March 1 is the delinquency date for the preceding year's bill, and February 28 is the last day to pay without interest.

faqs.q: What is the Tennessee transfer tax?
faqs.a: The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price. The buyer pays it, and the county register of deeds collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that is in foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes, if you close before the sale date. Newspaper notice must run at least 20 days before the sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house without probate?
faqs.a: A small estate affidavit covers personal property up to $50,000 and cannot transfer title to real estate. A house normally needs a personal representative with court authority.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption lower my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Tennessee's homestead exemption of up to $35,000 for an individual protects a home from certain creditors. It does not apply against public taxes.

faqs.q: Which Tennessee counties use the landlord and tenant act?
faqs.a: The act applies to counties with more than 75,000 people by the 2010 census, including Davidson, Shelby and Knox.

faqs.q: What does as-is mean in a cash sale?
faqs.a: The buyer takes the house in its present condition, so you skip repairs and cleaning.
